filing-20261001-5390.point: The commenter names four priorities for FERC's work on large loads such as data centers.
filing-20261001-5390.quote: keep transparency, cost responsibility, reliable planning, and protection of existing customers at the center of its consideration of rapidly growing large loads such as data centers.

filing-20260910-4000.point: Spartz says she cannot get clear numbers on energy, water and cost for large Indiana data center projects, partly because of nondisclosure agreements.
filing-20260910-4000.quote: Non-disclosure agreements and confidentiality arrangements have further limited transparency on matters affecting Indiana’s grid, water resources, taxpayers, and utility customers.

filing-20260910-4000.point: Meta announced a data center campus of more than $10 billion and about 1 GW at LEAP.
filing-20260910-4000.quote: Meta announced plans for a more than $10 billion data-center campus at LEAP, with 10 planned data centers and approximately 1 GW of capacity.

filing-20260910-4000.point: MISO planning documents put LEAP demand near 1,200 MW, with Wabash Valley Phase 2 transmission at about $345 million and Phase 1 at about $222 million.
filing-20260910-4000.quote: MISO planning documents estimate total LEAP demand at approximately 1,200 MW.

filing-20260910-4000.point: She summarizes FERC's MISO findings on cost shifting, Network Upgrade transparency, Cost Recovery Agreements and protections against stranded costs.
filing-20260910-4000.quote: FERC directed MISO and its transmission owners to address cost shifting, Network Upgrade transparency, Cost Recovery Agreements, financial protections against stranded infrastructure costs, and alternatives to traditional Network Upgrades

filing-20260910-4000.point: She requests project-level cost data and the enforceable protections that guard customers if projected loads do not materialize.
filing-20260910-4000.quote: Cost Recovery Agreements, minimum-demand commitments, financial guarantees, collateral, take-or-pay provisions, and other protections against stranded costs if projected loads are delayed, reduced, or never materialize.

filing-20260814-5198.point: OMS says many resource adequacy and affordability measures sit in state proceedings that MISO's report does not reflect.
filing-20260814-5198.quote: many important resource adequacy and affordability policy and implementation issues are being addressed through state proceedings and utility-specific processes

filing-20260814-5198.point: OMS says large load growth does not signal failure of the existing state and MISO resource adequacy framework.
filing-20260814-5198.quote: these challenges do not indicate a failure of the states and their collaboration with MISO’s underlying resource adequacy framework

filing-20260814-5198.point: OMS calls for planning that evaluates load additions with rigor comparable to new generation.
filing-20260814-5198.quote: planning processes that evaluate load additions using a level of rigor comparable to that applied to new generation resources

filing-20260814-5198.point: OMS cites state tariffs, special contracts and statutes that guard against cost shifting from new large loads.
filing-20260814-5198.quote: state commissions are implementing retail tariffs, approving special contracts, requiring resource adequacy demonstrations, establishing interruptible service requirements

filing-20260814-5198.point: OMS says existing interconnection processes should stay primary, with expedited paths narrowly tailored.
filing-20260814-5198.quote: existing interconnection processes should remain the primary pathway for connecting new resources

filing-20260812-5036.point: Sparkfund says aggregators and utilities in MISO can deploy distributed resources as capacity today under existing participation models.
filing-20260812-5036.quote: aggregators and utilities within MISO are able to deploy distributed resources as capacity today using the existing participation models.

filing-20260812-5036.point: Minnesota approved Xcel's Capacity*Connect: up to 200 MW of distribution-sited batteries by the end of 2028, with potential for 500 MW by 2031.
filing-20260812-5036.quote: to deploy up to 200 MW of front-of-the-meter, distribution-sited 1-3 MW battery energy storage systems (BESS) by the end of 2028

filing-20260812-5036.point: Google's Pine Island, MN agreement includes $50 million toward the battery portfolio for matched capacity credits.
filing-20260812-5036.quote: Google’s new Pine Island, MN data center facility has entered an Electric Service Agreement that includes $50 million towards Xcel’s Capacity*Connect battery portfolio

filing-20260812-5036.point: Xcel's compliance filing shows average residential savings of about $0.13 per month, rising to about $0.17 with Google's contribution.
filing-20260812-5036.quote: Capacity*Connect will deliver average residential bill savings of approximately $0.13 per month over the twenty-year analysis period

filing-20260812-5036.point: Sparkfund says several utilities each deploying 200-500 MW could total gigawatts in MISO.
filing-20260812-5036.quote: multiple utilities deploying 200-500 MW of utility-owned and operated distributed capacity could amount to gigawatts across the MISO footprint

filing-20260807-5199.point: AMP says the motion fails the Show Cause Order's abeyance standards, so FERC has grounds to deny it.
filing-20260807-5199.quote: The Motion fails to provide the information required by the Commission’s June 18 Show Cause Order in the event abeyance is sought

filing-20260807-5199.point: AMP names the missing protections: disclosure of upgrades and costs, cost recovery agreements, financial security and stranded-cost protection.
filing-20260807-5199.quote: public disclosure of large-load-driven network upgrades and their costs, cost recovery agreements, financial security requirements, and protection of existing transmission customers from stranded costs

filing-20260807-5199.point: AMP calls MISO's roadmap a few lines with a vague November filing.
filing-20260807-5199.quote: This falls well short of the detailed roadmap to compliance that the Commission required to justify abeyance.

filing-20260807-5199.point: AMP says upgrade costs are likely in the billions and MISO has presented no cost proposals in the stakeholder process.
filing-20260807-5199.quote: Costs associated with transmission upgrades to serve large loads are likely to be in the billions of dollars.

filing-20260807-5199.point: AMP says municipal and cooperative transmission-dependent utilities are not protected by state commissions because zonal cost allocation is wholesale.
filing-20260807-5199.quote: Transmission dependent utilities such as municipalities and cooperatives are not protected by state utility commissions and retail tariffs

filing-20260807-5199.point: AMP proposes three directives to MISO.
filing-20260807-5199.quote: bring forward a specific proposal to meet its obligations under the Show Cause Order to address cost transparency and cost shifting within the next twenty days

filing-20260807-5216.point: CEBA says abeyance gives time for collaboration instead of a rushed proposal that shifts debate into the docket.
filing-20260807-5216.quote: as opposed to a rushed proposal that would unnecessarily shift stakeholder debate to the Commission docket.

filing-20260807-5216.point: CEBA says 90 days would not materially slow reform.
filing-20260807-5216.quote: a 90-day extension would not materially impede the Commission’s objectives for advancing reforms quickly

filing-20260807-5216.point: CEBA asks for expedited grant, tied to MISO's mid-November filings.
filing-20260807-5216.quote: CEBA respectfully requests that the Commission grant the motion in an expedited manner.

filing-20260807-5186.point: OMS supports abeyance because the issues are interconnected and suited to a stakeholder process followed by section 205 filings.
filing-20260807-5186.quote: the issues identified by the Commission’s Show Cause Order are significant, highly interconnected, and best addressed through a coordinated stakeholder process

filing-20260807-5186.point: OMS conditions its support on full treatment of the Commission's issues and no prejudgment of resolution.
filing-20260807-5186.quote: Granting abeyance should not narrow the scope of the Commission’s inquiry or prejudge whether any particular issue has been adequately resolved

filing-20260807-5186.point: OMS lists the issues it wants addressed, including cost transparency, cost shifting if load does not materialize, flexible service and alternative transmission technologies.
filing-20260807-5186.quote: addressing the potential for inappropriate cost shifting when anticipated load does not ultimately materialize or materializes at a different scale or schedule than expected

filing-20260807-5186.point: OMS says MISO's stakeholder workstreams so far have favored issues supported by parties interested in developing and serving large loads.
filing-20260807-5186.quote: workstreams prioritized by MISO and stakeholders to date have been limited to those issues supported by parties largely interested in developing and serving large loads.

motion-el26-70-miso-abeyance.point: The movants say the stakeholder process needs the 90 days to craft section 205 filings answering the order.
motion-el26-70-miso-abeyance.quote: The Motion is necessary to permit MISO and the MISO Transmission Owners to continue the MISO stakeholder process to develop and submit FPA section

motion-el26-70-miso-abeyance.point: MISO says some issues in the order were not in its original workplan, and the 60-day deadline blocks stakeholder development.
motion-el26-70-miso-abeyance.quote: The current, imminent compliance deadline in the Show Cause Order effectively prohibits the full development and robust consideration of any potential stakeholder solutions to integrating large loads.

motion-el26-70-miso-abeyance.point: Planned filings: a Zero Injection Generator Interconnection Agreement, a large load definition, interconnection reliability requirements, a firm step-up service and a parallel load and resource study (LARS).
motion-el26-70-miso-abeyance.quote: a parallel study process for large load and generation resources (i.e., Load Addition and Resource Study process or “LARS”)

motion-el26-70-miso-abeyance.point: MISO expects to file the ZGIA by the end of August.
motion-el26-70-miso-abeyance.quote: MISO expects to submit the ZGIA filing by the end of August.

motion-el26-70-miso-abeyance.point: LARS would study load and generation in parallel within 120 days and address the order's proximate generation concern.
motion-el26-70-miso-abeyance.quote: The studies will be run in parallel, and will finish at approximately the same time—within 120 days

motion-el26-70-miso-abeyance.point: MISO expects to file the firm service step-up Tariff revisions by November 16, 2026, or earlier if feasible.
motion-el26-70-miso-abeyance.quote: MISO expects to make a section 205 filing proposing Tariff revisions incorporating the firm service step-up option by November 16, 2026, or earlier, if feasible.

motion-el26-70-miso-abeyance.point: The Large Load Working Group has six scheduled meetings before the abeyance ends.
motion-el26-70-miso-abeyance.quote: the LLWG is scheduled to meet six times between the date of this filing and the end of the requested abeyance period

filing-20260728-5083.point: Wabash says it does not dispute the need to address large and co-located load service.
filing-20260728-5083.quote: WVPA desires to clarify that it does not dispute the need for the Commission to address issues surrounding service to large load and co-located load

filing-20260728-5083.point: Wabash says it left public utility status on January 1, 2025, as an entity owned by exempt cooperatives.
filing-20260728-5083.quote: it ceased to be a public utility on January 1, 2025 because it became exempt from the Federal Power Act

filing-20260728-5083.point: Wabash says it is similarly situated to the non-jurisdictional owners listed in footnote 11.
filing-20260728-5083.quote: WVPA is a PTO within MISO, however, it is a PTO that is similarly situated to all of the other non-jurisdictional entities listed in footnote 11 of the Order.

filing-20260728-5083.point: Wabash cites FERC's treatment of a similar ISO-NE request and its CAISO rescission precedent.
filing-20260728-5083.quote: an errata to the Order would be consistent with the Commission’s treatment of a request from a similarly situated non-jurisdictional entity in Docket No. EL26-72-000

filing-20260728-5083.point: Wabash asks for the two corrections and, alternatively, rescission as to Wabash.
filing-20260728-5083.quote: removes WVPA from the caption of Docket No. EL26-70-000, which intended to identify only MISO and jurisdictional PTOs; and (2) adds WVPA in the list of non-jurisdictional PTO entities in footnote 11.

report-el26-70-miso.point: MISO says its current framework suits traditional load growth but new large loads bring challenges that need new tools.
report-el26-70-miso.quote: The unique nature of certain new large loads and the need to help ensure speed to power, however, brings new challenges that require MISO to continue to work with its states

report-el26-70-miso.point: MISO says LSEs should not build local transmission or generation for speculative loads.
report-el26-70-miso.quote: It is not prudent for load serving entities to build local transmission, or generation, for speculative loads.

report-el26-70-miso.point: MISO plans a Zero Injection Generator Interconnection Agreement for generation serving load at the same substation.
report-el26-70-miso.quote: facilitate faster interconnection of generation resources that serve only Load connected to the same substation and will not inject energy further onto the Transmission System.

report-el26-70-miso.point: MISO will develop a Large Load Parallel Study Process and file it under section 205.
report-el26-70-miso.quote: intends to submit a Section 205 filing to the Commission codifying the Large Load Parallel Study Process in the Tariff

report-el26-70-miso.point: MISO says states are primarily responsible for resource adequacy.
report-el26-70-miso.quote: States are primarily responsible for resource adequacy, which involves overseeing Load Serving Entities (“LSEs”) and ensuring LSEs plan for and secure enough power

report-el26-70-miso.point: The 2026 OMS-MISO Survey projects sufficient capacity for five years while LSE load growth runs 3.1% to 5.1% a year.
report-el26-70-miso.quote: Compound Annual Growth Rate (“CAGR”) projected between 3.1% and 5.1% over five years.

report-el26-70-miso.point: ERAS has moved 40 projects and 19 GW through accelerated interconnection.
report-el26-70-miso.quote: To date, 40 projects and 19 GWs of generation have completed the accelerated ERAS process

report-el26-70-miso.point: MISO says JTIQ upgrades unlock more than 28 GW of interconnection capability on the MISO-SPP seam.
report-el26-70-miso.quote: unlock more than 28 GW of new interconnection capability along the MISO‑SPP seam

filing-20260624-5016.point: The commenter ties the filing to the June 18 orders directing evaluation of alternative transmission technologies.
filing-20260624-5016.quote: the Commission's June 18, 2026 orders directing RTOs to evaluate alternative transmission technologies and upgrades to accommodate large loads

filing-20260624-5016.point: The commenter asked ATC to evaluate reconductoring instead of the $350 million Viridon WISE line and says ATC did not answer.
filing-20260624-5016.quote: the incumbent utility refused to provide an answer and deflected the inquiry to the greenfield developer.

filing-20260624-5016.point: The commenter presents the emails as evidence that cheaper grid-enhancing options go unevaluated.
filing-20260624-5016.quote: incumbent utilities and developers in the MISO footprint are actively avoiding the evaluation of cost-effective Grid-Enhancing Technologies and existing line upgrades
